structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: Reliance Industries Limited notifies BSE and NSE about sending the notice of its 48th Annual General Meeting (Post-IPO) and Integrated Annual Report for FY 2024-25 via electronic mode to members and debenture holders. It provides website links for the notice and annual report, and mentions a separate letter with web-link for members without registered email, per SEBI Regulation 36(1)(b). The letter includes company contact details, a copy list to various exchanges and depositories, and is signed by the Company Secretary.

structure.title: CIN: L17110MH1973PLC019786
key_items: RESOLVED FURTHER THAT; RESOLVED FURTHER THAT
structure.summary: This notice announces Reliance Industries Limited's 48th Annual General Meeting (Post-IPO) to be held on August 29, 2025, via video conferencing. The ordinary business includes adopting the audited financial statements (standalone and consolidated) for FY2024-25, declaring a dividend of ₹5.50 per equity share, and appointing Shri Nikhil R. Meswani and Ms. Isha M. Ambani as directors retiring by rotation. Special business covers ratifying Cost Auditors' remuneration for FY2025-26, appointing Dr. K. R. Chandratre as Secretarial Auditor for five years, and approving material related party transactions of the company and its subsidiaries. The notice includes company contact details and is signed by the Company Secretary.

structure.title: AGM Notice Notes: VC/OAVM Meeting, Director Reappointments, Electronic Report Dispatch
key_items: Despatch of Annual Report through Electronic Mode:
structure.summary: The page outlines AGM notes: MCA Circulars permit VC/OAVM meetings with deemed venue at registered office; Section 102 statement and additional information annexed; no proxy/attendance slip or route map due to virtual format; directors Nikhil Meswani and Isha Ambani retire by rotation with re-appointment resolutions and related interest disclosures; director details in Annexure. It also covers electronic dispatch of the Annual Report per MCA Circulars and Listing Regulations, including web-link letters for unregistered emails, availability on company/exchange/registrar websites, and instructions for members to register/update email addresses for demat and physical holdings.

structure.title: AGM VC/OAVM Joining and E-Voting Procedures
key_items: Procedure for joining the AGM through VC / OAVM:
Members are requested to follow the procedure given below:; Enter the login credentials (i.e., User ID and password provided in the accompanying communication) and click on “Login”.
Members are requested to follow the procedure given below:
Enter the login credentials (i.e., User ID and password provided in the accompanying communication) and click on “Login”.
Procedure for ‘remote e-voting’ and e-voting at the AGM (‘Insta Poll’):
structure.summary: The text outlines procedures for members to join the AGM via VC/OAVM, including login steps (using JioEvents link and credentials), password retrieval, speaker registration (Aug 8-16, 2025) with selection criteria, chat box for queries, first-come-first-served attendance, and requirements for institutional/corporate members to submit authorization documents. It notes that facility opens 30 minutes early, provides KFinTech contact details for assistance, clarifies joint holder voting (higher in order), states VC/OAVM attendees count for quorum, encourages institutional investors to attend, and introduces the procedure for remote e-voting and Insta Poll.

structure.title: 13. A. E-VOTING FACILITY:
key_items: B. INFORMATION AND INSTRUCTIONS RELATING TO E-VOTING:
INFORMATION AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR REMOTE E-VOTING BY INDIVIDUAL MEMBERS HOLDING SHARES OF THE COMPANY IN DEMAT MODE
structure.summary: The text outlines e-voting facilities for a company's AGM, including remote e-voting and Insta Poll at the meeting, with KFinTech as the agency. It specifies the voting period (August 24-28, 2025), cut-off date (August 22, 2025), and appointment of scrutinizers. Instructions cover voting rights, single mode voting, and procedures for individual demat members via NSDL and CDSL, including login steps. It also addresses restrictions on changing votes and eligibility based on the cut-off date, and provides detailed login procedures for demat members.

structure.title: PROCEDURE TO LOGIN THROUGH WEBSITES OF DEPOSITORIES
structure.summary: The section provides comprehensive e-voting login procedures for Reliance Industries Limited shareholders through NSDL and CDSL, including registration for unregistered users, direct access via depository websites, and demat account logins, all redirecting to KFinTech for voting. It covers password recovery options, helpdesk contacts, and detailed instructions for members receiving e-voting emails, including login, password change, and profile updates. Emphasis is placed on password confidentiality. Voting instructions cover selecting event numbers, entering share quantities, casting votes, and institutional submission requirements. Additional topics include Insta Poll voting, result declaration, document inspection procedures, IEPF compliance, dividend payment details, TDS rules for resident and non-resident members, and SEBI-mandated dematerialization and personal detail update procedures.

nodes.title: E-Voting Login Procedures for NSDL and CDSL
key_items: Users may directly access the e-Voting module of CDSL as per the following procedure:
Procedure to login through their demat accounts / Website of Depository Participant
nodes.summary: The document outlines procedures for shareholders to access e-Voting for Reliance Industries Limited through NSDL and CDSL. It covers registration for IDeAS e-Services (NSDL) and Easi/Easiest (CDSL) for unregistered users, direct access to e-Voting modules via NSDL and CDSL websites with login steps, and access through demat accounts or Depository Participant websites. Each method redirects users to the KFinTech e-Voting page for casting votes without further authentication.

nodes.title: Members who are unable to retrieve User ID / Password are advised to use “Forgot User ID” / “Forgot Password” options available on the websites of Depositories / Depository Participants.
nodes.summary: The text provides guidance for members unable to retrieve their User ID or Password, advising them to use "Forgot User ID" or "Forgot Password" options on Depositories or Depository Participants' websites. It lists contact details for technical issues on NSDL and CDSL websites, including NSDL helpdesk email and phone, and CDSL helpdesk email and phone. It also references a document section titled "Information and Instructions for Remote E-Voting" for certain member categories, with sub-items (a) through (g).

nodes.title: In case a member receives an e-mail from the Company / KFinTech [for members whose e-mail address is registered with the Company / Depository Participant(s)]:
nodes.summary: The text provides instructions for members receiving an e-voting email from the Company or KFinTech. It details launching the browser and visiting https://evoting.kfintech.com, logging in with credentials where the User ID is the E-Voting Event Number plus Folio No. or DP ID Client ID, and using an existing password if registered. It offers assistance via the website or toll-free number 1800 309 4001 on working days from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. IST. After login, users must change their password on first login, meeting complexity requirements (minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, numeric, and special character), and update contact details like mobile number and email. Users can also set a secret question and answer for password recovery.

nodes.title: It is strongly recommended that you do not share your password with any other person and that you take utmost care to keep your password confidential.
nodes.summary: The text covers e-voting instructions for Reliance Industries Limited, emphasizing password confidentiality and re-login with new credentials. It details selecting the E-Voting Event Number, entering share numbers for FOR/AGAINST/ABSTAIN, and separate voting for multiple folios. It explains vote submission, confirmation, and finality. Institutional members must submit board resolutions and authorizations to the Scrutiniser. It provides steps for unregistered email holders to generate login credentials, including physical and demat modes, and methods to retrieve forgotten credentials via SMS, online, phone, or email. It also covers Insta Poll voting, contact details for assistance, e-voting result declaration, inspection of documents, and notes on resolutions deemed passed.

nodes.title: E-Voting, Insta Poll Instructions, and Contact Details
key_items: (viii) INFORMATION AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR INSTA POLL: Facility to vote through Insta Poll will be made available on the Meeting page (after you log into the Meeting)
Members are requested to note the following contact details for addressing e-voting related grievances:
Subject to receipt of requisite number of votes, the Resolutions proposed in this Notice shall be deemed to have been passed on the date of the Meeting, i.e., Friday, August 29, 2025.
nodes.summary: The page provides detailed instructions for e-voting, including how to cast votes via Insta Poll during the meeting, updating mobile and email in user profiles, and retrieving forgotten user IDs and passwords via SMS, online, phone, or email. It lists contact details for e-voting grievances and assistance from KFinTech, including a toll-free number and email. It explains that the Scrutiniser will consolidate votes from Insta Poll and remote e-voting, with results announced by September 1, 2025, and placed on company and KFinTech websites, communicated to stock exchanges, and displayed at the registered office. Resolutions are deemed passed on the meeting date, August 29, 2025, subject to requisite votes.

nodes.title: Procedure for Inspection of Documents:
nodes.summary: This text outlines procedures for document inspection for an AGM. It states that the Register of Directors and Key Managerial Personnel, and Register of Contracts or Arrangements, plus a Secretarial Auditor certificate regarding the Reliance Industries Limited Employees' Stock Option Scheme 2017, are available electronically for member inspection during the AGM. All documents cited in the Notice are available electronically without fee from the Notice circulation date to the AGM date; members requesting inspection can email rilagm@ril.com with folio or DP ID/Client ID. Additionally, members seeking information on accounts or AGM matters must email the company by August 22, 2025, and the company will respond appropriately.

nodes.title: IEPF Related Information:
nodes.summary: The text details IEPF compliance: the Company transferred unpaid/unclaimed dividends up to FY 2016-17 to the IEPF, with details on the IEPF Authority and Company websites. Unpaid/unclaimed dividends as of March 31, 2025, are on the Company website. It notes that during FY 2024-25, shares with dividends unpaid/unclaimed for seven consecutive years were transferred to the IEPF Authority as of September 25, 2024, with details on both websites. Members can claim back shares and dividends from the IEPF Authority, and procedures are provided via the Shareholders' Referencer, IEPF website, or KFinTech. A table lists declaration dates and last claim dates before IEPF transfer for FY 2018-19 to 2023-24, and it mentions the FY 2017-18 last claim date was August 4, 2025, with transfer in process.

nodes.title: Dividend Related Information
key_items: Tax Deductible at Source (TDS) / Withholding tax
nodes.summary: The text outlines dividend payment details: dividends approved at the AGM will be paid within a week to members on the Register of Members as of the Record Date (August 14, 2025), including dematerialized shares via NSDL/CDSL beneficial owners. Members must update bank details with Depository Participants for electronic payment. For physical shares, SEBI mandates electronic payment only after furnishing PAN, contact details, bank account, and specimen signature to the Company/KFinTech, with reference to SEBI FAQs. Tax Deductible at Source (TDS)/withholding tax will be applied at prescribed rates based on residential status and submitted documents; members must update their residential status by the Record Date to ensure correct tax rates.

nodes.title: A. Resident members:
key_items: A.1 Tax Deductible at Source for Resident members
nodes.summary: The text outlines tax deduction at source (TDS) rules for resident members' dividends, covering: A.1 with rates and documents for valid PAN (10%), invalid/missing PAN or Aadhaar linkage (20%), lower/nil tax deduction certificates under Section 197, and Rule 37BA benefits; deadlines of August 14, 2025 for PAN updates and certificate submission; and A.2 listing documents for nil TDS, including Forms 15G/15H, exemptions under Sections 194 and 196, Category I/II AIFs, recognized provident/superannuation/gratuity funds, National Pension Scheme, and other exemptions with valid documentary evidence.

nodes.title: B. Non-Resident members:
nodes.summary: This text details withholding tax rules for non-resident members receiving dividends. It lists rates and required documents for FIIs/FPIs (20% or treaty rate), Indian branches of foreign banks (NIL with declaration, else 35%), lower/NIL tax certificate holders, exempt entities, and Rule 37BA beneficial owners. Members must submit documents by August 14, 2025, to avail beneficial rates. It also covers TDS certificate issuance, online document upload, NSDL facility for institutional members, verification conditions, refund option for higher deduction, TDS exemption for resident individuals up to ₹10,000, PAN update requirements, indemnity for inaccurate declarations, and a disclaimer to consult tax advisors.

nodes.title: Other Information
nodes.summary: The text outlines SEBI-mandated dematerialization for securities transfer, advises members to verify holdings periodically, and details procedures for updating personal details (address, email, mobile, PAN, nomination, bank) for demat shares via Depository Participants/NSDL and for physical shares via KFinTech forms (ISR-1, ISR-2, SH-13, SH-14, ISR-3). It instructs NRIs to report residential status changes, notes Listing Regulations requiring demat for transfer/transmission/transposition, and SEBI circular mandating demat issuance for service requests (duplicate certificates, unclaimed suspense claims, renewal/exchange, endorsement, sub-division, consolidation, transmission, transposition) via Form ISR-4. It provides links to forms, shareholders’ referencer, and a feedback form, and directs submissions to KFinTech.

structure.title: STATEMENT PURSUANT TO SECTION 102(1) OF THE COMPANIES ACT, 2013 AND ADDITIONAL INFORMATION AS REQUIRED UNDER THE SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA (LISTING OBLIGATIONS AND DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS) REGULATIONS, 2015 AND CIRCULARS ISSUED THEREUNDER
structure.summary: The notice covers three agenda items: Item 5 seeks member ratification of the remuneration of Cost Auditors for FY 2025-26, as approved by the Board and Audit Committee, with details of ten auditors and fees. Item 6 proposes appointment of Dr. K. R. Chandratre as Secretarial Auditor for a five-year term, outlining his qualifications, experience, and proposed remuneration. Items 7 and 8 seek approval for related party transactions exceeding specified thresholds, describing the company's business, governance process for such transactions, Audit Committee oversight, and the materiality thresholds under SEBI regulations. All items require Ordinary Resolutions, with no director interest.

structure.title: A1. Transactions between the Company and Reliance Consumer Products Limited
key_items: B1. Transactions between Reliance Consumer Products Limited and Metro Cash and Carry India Limited
structure.summary: The notice details two related party transaction (RPT) proposals. Section A1 covers transactions between Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) and Reliance Consumer Products Limited (RCPL), a step-down subsidiary, including RIL's sale of petrochemical products to RCPL, purchase of FMCG goods from RCPL, and investments/loans/guarantees to RCPL. It specifies relationships, transaction types, tenures (FY2025-26 to FY2029-30 for goods, FY2025-26 to FY2026-27 for investments), estimated values (up to ₹6,000 crore for sales, ₹600 crore for purchases, ₹10,000 crore for investments), percentage of RIL's and RCPL's turnover, loan terms, justification, and director interest. Section B1 covers transactions between RCPL and Metro Cash and Carry India Limited (METRO India), fellow step-down subsidiaries, involving RCPL's procurement of goods from METRO India and METRO India's marketing support services. It provides relationship details, transaction types, tenures (FY2025-26 to FY2029-30), estimated values (up to ₹1,000 crore for goods, ₹100 crore for services), turnover percentages, justification, prior member approval, and director interest. The notice seeks member approval for both sets of transactions and allied matters.

structure.title: B2. Transactions between Jio Platforms Limited and JioStar India Private Limited
structure.summary: This related party transaction statement details proposed transactions between Jio Platforms Limited (JPL) and JioStar India Private Limited, both fellow subsidiaries of Reliance Industries Limited. It covers the parties' relationship and shareholding, related directors/KMP, and four transaction types: Managed IT services (cost-plus), CDN services (market rates), customer acquisition and advertising (market rates), and content provision for bundled offerings (market rates). It specifies estimated values for FY2025-26 and up to FY2029-30, their percentage of the Company's consolidated turnover and each subsidiary's turnover, confirms no loans or valuation reports, justifies each transaction's benefits, and notes director interest and deemed concern.

structure.title: B3. Transactions between JioStar India Private Limited and GTPL Hathway Limited
key_items: B4. Transactions between Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited and Reliance Jio Infocomm UK Limited
structure.summary: The text details two related party transaction (RPT) proposals from Reliance Industries Limited's notice: B3 covers transactions between JioStar India Private Limited and GTPL Hathway Limited, including relationship details, transaction types (channel distribution and placement services), estimated values (₹1,450 crore for FY2025-26 and up to ₹2,900 crore for subsequent years for GTPL's subscription payments; ₹1,050 crore for FY2025-26 and up to ₹2,100 crore for JioStar's payments to GTPL), turnover percentages, justification, and director interests. B4 covers transactions between Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited and Reliance Jio Infocomm UK Limited, including relationship, services (IP transit, ILD voice, business support), pricing terms, estimated values (₹1,270 crore for FY2025-26 and up to ₹3,100 crore for subsequent years for RJIUK's services; ₹1,700 crore for FY2025-26 and up to ₹4,000 crore for RJIL's services), turnover percentages, justification, and director interests. Both sections include approval requests for five financial years (FY2025-26 to FY2029-30), relevant regulatory compliance, and voting instructions.

structure.title: Annexure to the Notice dated August 6, 2025
structure.summary: This notice annexure details two directors retiring by rotation: Nikhil R. Meswani and Isha M. Ambani. For each, it provides age, qualifications, experience, terms of re-appointment, remuneration (last drawn and proposed), date of first appointment, shareholding, relationships with other directors/KMP, board meeting attendance, other directorships, committee memberships, and recent resignations. It includes their resumes, shareholding details, and family relationships. The document also contains RIL's contact information, a company overview, and AGM participation details.

structure.title: Pursue your goals even in the face of difficulties, and convert adversities into opportunities. Shri. Dhirubhai H. Ambani
structure.summary: This text includes an inspirational quote from Dhirubhai Ambani and highlights key achievements: being the first Indian company to cross consolidated total equity of over ₹10,00,000 crore, exports of ₹2,83,719 crore, CSR contribution of ₹2,156 crore, and 4,03,303 people. It notes rankings: #88 Fortune Global 500, #49 Forbes Global 2000, and among TIME100 most influential companies 2024, and champions Make in India. A forward-looking statement disclaimer is provided. The table of contents covers corporate overview, management discussion and analysis (financial performance, business segments: retail, digital services, media and entertainment, oil to chemicals, oil and gas, risk and governance, awards), integrated approach to ESG (governance, net carbon zero, climate disclosures, natural, human, manufactured, intellectual, social and relationship capital, independent assurance), reporting suite 2024-25, a quote from Mukesh Ambani, governance (corporate governance report, board’s report), financial statements (standalone, consolidated), and links to CSR and BRSR reports.

structure.title: RELIANCE AT A GLANCE
structure.summary: The text provides an overview of Reliance Industries, highlighting its multiple growth engines: Retail (revenue up 7.9%, EBITDA up 8.6%), Digital Services (revenue up 15.9%, EBITDA up 14.7%), Media & Entertainment (revenue up 74.3%, EBITDA up 139.6%), Oil to Chemicals (revenue up 11.0%, EBITDA up 11.9%), and Oil and Gas (revenue up 3.2%, EBITDA up 4.9%), with figures for FY2025 and key offerings. It also covers stakeholder value creation, including total value added, contributions to national exchequer, reinvestment, debt providers, employee benefits, equity capital, and society, with FY2025 and FY2024 comparisons. Finally, it lists sustainable growth enablers such as technology and consumer-centric platforms, project management, access to capital, and diversification.

structure.title: What is Good for India is Good for Reliance
key_items: Movement in Key Financial Ratios; Liquidity Management; Credit Rating; Way Forward
structure.summary: The text is Reliance Industries' Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, featuring Chairman Mukesh Ambani's letter to shareholders. It covers Reliance's evolution into a national institution, its adaptation to digital disruption, and its alignment with India's growth. It highlights FY25 financial performance with revenue, EBITDA, and net profit figures, and details segment performance across Retail, Digital Services, Media, O2C, Oil & Gas, and New Energy. The report outlines four new growth engines, emphasizes values, people, and vision, and includes 10-year financial highlights, management discussion and analysis of the operating environment, performance overview, net debt, capex, standalone results, key financial ratios, liquidity, fund raising, credit ratings, and a business overview of Retail.

structure.title: Retail
structure.summary: The text covers RIL's financial performance and review, including key ratio movements (net capital turnover improvement, operating margin and return on net worth declines), liquidity and capital resources, macroeconomic conditions in India, fund raising through multi-currency offshore and green ECA facilities, liquidity management, credit ratings, and future outlook. It then provides a business overview of Reliance Retail, detailing its strategic objective, industry overview, financial performance (revenue, EBITDA, store count), strategic progress across segments (consumer electronics, fashion and lifestyle, grocery, consumer brands, JioMart and Milkbasket, connectivity), SCOT analysis, and outlook.

structure.title: Digital Services
structure.summary: This text covers the Digital Services and Media & Entertainment segments of Reliance Industries. For Digital Services, it outlines Jio's business overview, strategic objective, industry trends (broadband, 5G, AI), regulatory developments (spectrum auction, data protection, TRAI guidelines), financial performance, leadership in technology transitions, market position in mobility and fixed broadband, ecosystem approach, SCOT analysis, AI initiatives (JioBrain), and outlook. For Media & Entertainment, it details the creation of JioStar, strategic objective, industry growth drivers (digital, connected TVs, sports), TV entertainment performance, financials, digital success (JioHotstar), news business, SCOT analysis, and outlook.

structure.title: India’s Undisputed Content Powerhouse
structure.summary: The text covers two business overviews. Jio Studios' FY 2024-25 performance highlights over 40 films/web originals, dominance in Hindi box office with three top-five hits contributing 40%+ of India NBOC surpassing ₹1,000 crores, notable films like "Stree 2" (highest-grossing Hindi film), platform-agnostic storytelling across Netflix, Amazon Prime, ZEE5, etc., with record viewership for "Laapataa Ladies" and "Mrs.", soundtrack success, 65+ awards including 15 IIFA wins, international festival recognition, Oscar selection for "Laapataa Ladies," IMDb popularity, new moving logo, regional expansion in Marathi cinema, and upcoming projects. The Oil to Chemicals (O2C) business overview covers its portfolio (transportation fuels, polymers & elastomers, intermediates, polyesters), integrated assets and logistics, strategic objective to meet India's energy/materials demand with circular economy and Net Carbon Zero by 2035, key metrics (80.5 MMT throughput, 71.2 MMT production for sale, 29,985 people), and industry overview detailing FY 2024-25 transportation fuel demand/supply challenges, oil demand/supply figures, Brent price, refinery throughput, gasoline/diesel/jet fuel demand trends, key factors for 2025, Indian petroleum product demand at 239 MMTPA, and EV/CNG vehicle parc growth.

structure.title: OIL TO CHEMICALS
structure.summary: This management discussion covers O2C business performance across oil-to-chemicals, including polymers, elastomers, intermediates, polyesters, and transportation fuels. It details global and domestic demand trends, capacity additions, margin movements, and feedstock price changes for ethylene, polymers, elastomers, intermediates, and polyesters. The transportation fuel section discusses production increases, declining cracks, and Jio-bp's network expansion and sales growth. Financial performance shows revenue growth of 11.0% to ₹6,26,921 crore and EBITDA decline of 11.9% to ₹54,988 crore. A SCOT analysis outlines strengths, challenges, opportunities, and threats. Production meant for sale data by product is provided, along with an outlook on oil demand, refining margins, and downstream chemical demand growth in India.

structure.title: Oil and Gas
key_items: Powering a Net Carbon Zero Future; Strategic Objective: From Ambition to Execution; Business Updates
Powering a Net Carbon Zero Future
Strategic Objective: From Ambition to Execution
Risks and Response Strategic and Commercial Risks
structure.summary: This Management Discussion and Analysis covers the Oil and Gas business overview and Reliance's clean energy initiatives. For Oil and Gas, it details E&P industry performance including KG Basin and CBM production, strategic objectives, financials, portfolio, exploration strategy, SCOT analysis, legal issues, and outlook. It highlights production figures, revenue and EBITDA growth, and key focus areas like clean energy, brownfields, and digital technologies. The clean energy section outlines strategic objectives, global and Indian energy trends, business updates on the Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex (solar, battery, electrolyser), and Bio Energy (CBG plants). Finally, it covers Risk and Governance, including the Enterprise Risk Management framework, governance structure, and specific risks such as climate change and commodity prices, along with responses.

structure.title: RISK AND GOVERNANCE
key_items: Safety and Operational Risks; Compliance and Control Risks; Financial Risks; Insurance – Risk Mitigation
structure.summary: This Management Discussion and Analysis section covers Risk and Governance, detailing risk responses across multiple areas. It addresses supply disruption mitigation through diversified suppliers and operational stability. Customer experience and retention risks are managed via technology and omnichannel solutions. Oversight over investee companies and alliances focuses on compliance and strategic coherence. Talent scaling is supported through development programs. Data privacy and cybersecurity risks are mitigated with privacy-by-design and Zero Trust frameworks. Health, safety, and environmental risks are managed through digitalization and a zero-incident culture. Physical security and natural calamity risks involve audits and predictive analytics. Regulatory compliance uses a digitally integrated framework. Financial risks include treasury risks (foreign exchange, liquidity, interest rate, credit) with hedging and refinancing strategies, plus insurance as a risk mitigation tool.

structure.title: Major Awards and Recognitions
structure.summary: This text from the Management Discussion and Analysis section lists major awards and recognitions received by Reliance Industries and its subsidiaries. It covers leadership and innovation accolades, including rankings, brand value, workplace certifications, and innovation awards. It details recognitions in Retail, Consumer Electronics, Digital (Jio, Jio-bp, Jio Platforms), Fashion and Lifestyle, Grocery, and Media & Entertainment (Jio Hotstar, Jio Studios). It also includes awards for Reliance Foundation, HSE and Sustainability, and various manufacturing divisions. The awards span multiple categories such as business excellence, branding, technology, safety, sustainability, and employee choice.

structure.title: Integrated Approach to Sustainable Growth
structure.summary: The section outlines Reliance's integrated approach to sustainable growth, covering ESG governance with board oversight and material topics, a Net Carbon Zero by 2035 strategy including renewable energy and giga factories, natural capital management (emissions, biodiversity, waste, water), human capital (talent, health, safety, diversity, human rights, ethics), manufactured capital (deep-tech, asset management), intellectual capital (innovation, data privacy), social and relationship capital (community, customer satisfaction, supply chain), and assurance.

nodes.title: Integrated Approach to ESG Governance
nodes.summary: The text outlines Reliance's integrated approach to sustainable growth, guided by the belief that what is good for India is good for Reliance, driven by technology and innovation. It details the Integrated Report 2024-25 using the six capitals of the International Integrated Reporting Framework, adhering to standards like GRI, IIRC, GHG Protocol, IPCC AR5, and UN SDGs, covering ESG disclosures for O2C, Digital Services, and Retail. It describes ESG governance, including a 14-member Board, Board Committees (ESG, Audit, CSR, Stakeholders Relationship, Risk Management), and the sustainability governance structure with the ESG Committee comprising two executive directors and one independent director. It covers policies and Code of Conduct, anti-competitive behavior, stakeholder engagement, materiality approach (including double materiality), and lists 25 material topics spanning climate change, environmental impacts, energy efficiency, water management, raw material security, biodiversity, innovation, circular economy, supply chain, disaster preparedness, health and safety, diversity, customer satisfaction, data privacy, asset management, talent management, community development, labour management, human rights, business ethics, regulatory compliance, grievance redressal, risk management, economic performance, and code of conduct.

nodes.title: Making Significant Strides towards a Net Carbon Zero Future
nodes.summary: Reliance's strategy for achieving Net Carbon Zero by 2035 includes building 100 GW of renewable energy by 2030 and developing giga factories for an integrated renewable ecosystem. It covers the Net Carbon Zero strategy (backward integration, robust business model, scale), deep tech/R&D investments, and the Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex in Jamnagar with solar and battery giga-factories, electrolyser plans, and land in Kutch and Kandla. It details FY 2024-25 energy savings and renewable consumption, 2025 milestones (10 GW solar PV, 30 GWh battery), 2030 and 2035 targets, and clean energy transition initiatives including e-mobility and CO2 conversion. Climate-related disclosures are addressed through TCFD-aligned governance, risk management, strategy (including just transition), and metrics/targets.

nodes.title: Natural Capital
nodes.summary: Reliance's natural capital management covers governance via Board oversight and HSE/OMS policies with independent S&OR reviews; environmental impact management including air emissions (TPM, SOx, NOx, VOC) monitored by CEMS; climate change actions toward Net Carbon Zero by 2035, renewable energy, CBG expansion, and GHG emissions data for O2C/E&P and Jio; energy efficiency initiatives and renewable energy use; ecosystem and biodiversity efforts with greenbelts, saplings, and Vantara; waste management and circular economy including recycling and ISCC Plus certification; and water and effluent management with withdrawal, discharge, and recycling data.

nodes.title: Human Capital
nodes.summary: This document covers Reliance's human capital management for FY2024-25, aligned with BRSR principles and UN SDGs. It details the management approach rooted in the 10 Tenets of Institutional Leadership, emphasizing empathy, inclusivity, and human rights. Key areas include talent attraction and retention, highlighting over 1.9 lakh new hires and a total workforce exceeding 4 lakh, with recognition as a top employer. Health, safety, and well-being are addressed through HSE systems, the CASHE program, and significant investments. Diversity and inclusion efforts are outlined via the DE&I Charter, 5E framework, and various programs, with metrics on women in leadership. Talent management covers training and development initiatives, including CAP, FLYER, and digital learning. Labour management and human rights compliance are discussed, noting collective bargaining and human rights training. The text also covers business ethics, integrity, transparency, and the grievance redressal mechanism, including the Vigil Mechanism and Whistleblower Policy.

nodes.title: Manufactured Capital
nodes.summary: The text covers Reliance Industries' BRSR 2024-25 report sections on Manufactured Capital (deep-tech integration, business performance, raw material security, asset management), Intellectual Capital (innovation, IP portfolio, R&D focus areas, data privacy and cybersecurity), Social and Relationship Capital (community development, customer satisfaction, sustainable supply chain), Outlook, and an Independent Practitioner's Assurance Report with detailed assurance scope, responsibilities, procedures, and opinions on sustainability information.

structure.title: APPENDIX I
structure.summary: This appendix lists identified sustainability information subject to reasonable assurance, referencing GRI Standards disclosures. It covers energy consumption (total, renewable, non-renewable) and reduction; water withdrawal by source, discharge by destination, consumption and recycling; direct (Scope 1) and indirect (Scope 2) GHG emissions; air emissions (NOx, SOx, TPM, VOCs); waste diverted and directed to disposal; flared and vented hydrocarbons; and work-related injuries (LTIFR, hours worked). Boundaries include Oil to Chemicals (O2C) Entities, Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (RJIL), Reliance Retail Limited (RRL), and Reliance Projects & Property Management Services Limited (RPPMSL).

structure.title: APPENDIX II

The Oil & Gas segment achieved record revenue (₹25,211 crore, up 3.2%) and EBITDA (₹21,188 crore, up 4.9%) from KG-D6 and CBM fields, including additional well plans and MLW campaigns contributing 30% of India's production. It also details credit ratings, consolidated financial statements, subsidiary/JV/associate changes, material subsidiaries, secretarial standards, Directors' Responsibility Statement, corporate governance, BRSR, related party transactions, CSR initiatives (₹1,309 crore spent, 86 million lives touched), and risk management framework.

nodes.title: Standalone Financial Statement Notes: Current Investments and Trade Receivables
nodes.summary: The page presents notes 7 and 8 to the standalone financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025, with comparative figures for 31st March 2024. Note 7 covers current investments, detailing investments measured at amortised cost (collateral borrowing and lending obligation), at fair value through other comprehensive income (government securities, debentures/bonds, mutual funds), and at fair value through profit or loss (government securities, debentures/bonds, treasury bills, mutual funds, certificates of deposit, commercial papers), including totals, aggregate quoted and unquoted amounts, market value of quoted investments, collateral security disclosures, and a category-wise summary. Note 8 covers trade receivables, showing total unsecured considered good receivables and an ageing analysis by due date, credit risk, and disputed status.

nodes.title: 9. Cash and Cash Equivalents
nodes.summary: The text covers notes to Reliance Industries' standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It includes: Note 9 on cash and cash equivalents, detailing components, maturity analysis, and bank balances with unclaimed dividend and fixed deposits; Note 10 on other financial assets including deposits with related parties and receivables; Note 11 on taxation, presenting tax expenses, reconciliation with accounting profit, and effective tax rate; Note 12 on other current assets; and Note 13 on share capital, covering authorized, issued, and subscribed capital, bonus shares, forfeiture, shareholders holding over 5%, and promoter shareholding.

nodes.title: Standalone Financial Statement Notes: Other Financial Assets, Taxation, Other Current Assets
nodes.summary: The page presents three notes to the standalone financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025. Note 10 covers Other Financial Assets – Current, detailing deposits with related parties, other deposits, receivables from related parties, and others, including fair valuation of derivatives. Note 11 addresses Taxation, showing tax expenses recognized in profit and loss (current, deferred, total), a reconciliation of tax expense to accounting profit (profit before tax, applicable tax rate, computed tax expense, tax effects of disallowed expenses, additional allowances/deductions, current tax provision, deferred tax components related to property, plant and equipment, intangible assets, change in tax rate, financial assets and other items, deferred tax provision, total tax expense, and effective tax rate). Note 12 lists Other Current Assets (unsecured and considered good), comprising balances with customs, central excise, GST and state authorities, and others including prepaid expenses and claims receivable.

nodes.title: 13. Share Capital
nodes.summary: The text covers Note 13 on Share Capital, detailing authorized share capital (equity and preference shares) and issued/subscribed/paid-up equity capital for FY25 and FY24, including calls unpaid and bonus share allotment. It lists shareholders holding over 5% shares and promoter shareholding for Mukesh D Ambani. A reconciliation of outstanding shares shows movements from employee stock options, forfeiture, and bonus shares. It also includes reserves data: share-based payments and special economic zone reinvestment reserve, with comparative figures in crore.

nodes.title: 13.5 Pursuant to ‘Reliance Industries Limited Employees’ Stock Option Scheme 2017’ (ESOS-2017), options granted and remaining to be vested as at the end of the year is 66,088.
nodes.summary: The text covers notes to Reliance Industries Limited's standalone financial statements for FY2024-25, including: ESOS-2017 options outstanding (66,088); equity share rights and preferences; details of the rights issue (42,26,26,894 shares, calls, forfeitures); bonus issue of 676,61,86,449 shares (1:1) and increase in paid-up capital; other equity movements (capital reserve, securities premium, debenture redemption reserve, OCI reserves); borrowings (secured/unsecured NCDs, bonds, term loans) with maturity profiles and interest rates; other financial liabilities and provisions; deferred tax; revenue disaggregation; other income; changes in inventories; employee benefits expense and defined benefit plan disclosures; share-based payments (ESOS-2017 movement, fair value assumptions); finance costs; other expenses including CSR; earnings per share (basic/diluted, adjusted for bonus); related party disclosures (list of subsidiaries, transactions, balances); oil and gas joint arrangements and reserves; contingent liabilities and commitments (claims, guarantees, tax demands, SEBI matter); capital management (net gearing); financial instruments (fair value hierarchy, risk management, hedge accounting); segment information reference; loans/guarantees under Section 186; ratio analysis; other statutory information; events after reporting period (dividend recommendation); and approval of financial statements.

nodes.title: Opinion
nodes.summary: This independent auditor's report on Reliance Industries Limited's consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025 presents an unmodified opinion, confirming compliance with Ind AS and a true and fair view. It outlines the basis for opinion, auditor responsibilities, and management/board responsibilities. Five key audit matters are detailed: litigation matters (oil and gas disputes, RPL share trading), fair valuation of investments in Jio Digital Fibre, revenue recognition at RJIL and RRVL, IT systems and controls over financial reporting, and the business combination involving Star India. Other matters cover reliance on other auditors and unaudited financial information. The report also includes regulatory compliance statements under the Companies Act, 2013, covering internal financial controls, director qualifications, dividend compliance, and audit trail requirements, along with Annexure A on internal financial controls.

structure.title: “Annexure A”
structure.summary: The text covers auditor's reports on Reliance Industries Limited's consolidated financial statements. It details inherent limitations of internal financial controls, including collusion or management override risks, and notes future projections may become inadequate. The opinion affirms that the Parent, subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures incorporated in India have adequate and effectively operating internal financial controls as of March 31, 2025, based on ICAI guidance. Other Matters note the report relies on auditors' reports for 94 subsidiaries, 39 associates, and 20 joint ventures. Annexure B states no CARO qualifications or adverse remarks for audited companies. Signatures from Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP and Chaturvedi & Shah LLP are included.

structure.title: Consolidated Balance Sheet
structure.summary: The text presents the Consolidated Balance Sheet of Reliance Industries Limited as at 31st March 2025, with comparative figures for 31st March 2024. It details non-current assets including property, plant and equipment, spectrum, other intangible assets, goodwill, capital work-in-progress, financial assets, and deferred tax assets. Current assets such as inventories, investments, trade receivables, cash, loans, and other financial assets are also listed. The equity and liabilities section covers equity share capital, other equity, non-controlling interest, non-current liabilities (borrowings, lease liabilities, provisions, deferred tax liabilities), and current liabilities (borrowings, trade payables, provisions). The text includes auditor signatures, board member names and DINs, and reference to material accounting policies and notes. It is part of the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

structure.title: Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss
structure.summary: The text presents the consolidated statement of profit and loss for Reliance Industries Limited for the year ended March 31, 2025, with comparative figures for 2023-24. It details income from sales and services, GST recovered, revenue from operations, other income, and total income. Expenses include cost of materials, purchases, inventory changes, excise duty, employee benefits, finance costs, depreciation, and other expenses, leading to profit before tax and profit after tax. It also covers other comprehensive income, total comprehensive income, profit attributable to owners and non-controlling interest, and earnings per share (basic and diluted). The document includes signatures of auditors, CFO, company secretary, and board members, along with notes and accounting policies.

structure.title: Consolidated Statement of Changes in Equity
structure.summary: The text presents the Consolidated Statement of Changes in Equity for the year ended 31st March 2025, covering both Equity Share Capital and Other Equity. It details balances as of 1st April 2023, changes during 2023-24 and 2024-25, and balances as of 31st March 2024 and 2025. For Other Equity, it breaks down reserves and surplus (e.g., Capital Reserve, Debenture Redemption Reserve, Retained Earnings), other comprehensive income items, and total equity. It includes notes on rights issue, employee stock options, bonus shares, and dividends. The statement concludes with signatures of auditors, CFO, Company Secretary, and board members.

It includes the consolidated statement of cash flows, detailing operating, investing, and financing activities, along with a reconciliation of liabilities from financing activities. It also covers corporate information, material accounting policies (basis of preparation, principles of consolidation, and policies on property, plant and equipment, leases, intangible assets, inventories, provisions, taxes, share-based payments, foreign currencies, revenue recognition, and financial instruments), and notes on financial instruments including hedge accounting.

structure.title: Notes
structure.summary: The text lists Reliance Industries Limited's corporate governance details: board of directors (including chairman, non-executive, and executive directors), CFO, company secretary, auditors, registered office, various committees with members and chairs, bankers, and registrar. It also includes a shareholder letter announcing the 48th AGM on August 29, 2025, via video conferencing, providing links to the Integrated Annual Report and AGM Notice, and requesting shareholders to register email addresses with their depository or KFin Technologies, with contact details for queries.
